title: In Guangzhou, "Drinking Tea" Means a 3-Hour Feast | China Travel Expert
description:
In Cantonese it's called yum cha — literally "drink tea." But show up in Guangzhou and you'll find the tea is the smallest part of the morning.

Yum cha is a Cantonese tradition that took off in Guangzhou in the late 1800s: a pot of tea plus an endless parade of dim sum — steamed dumplings, buns, rice-noodle rolls and egg tarts, traditionally wheeled to your table on push carts. "Dim sum" (点心) means "to touch the heart," and the classic order is 一盅两件 — one pot of tea and two small dishes — though almost nobody stops at two. Breakfast here can stretch for hours.

🧭 Expert Tip: Go before 10am to beat the crowd, and start with har gow (shrimp dumplings) and char siu bao (BBQ-pork buns).
